# Mahāvaccha Sutta (MN 73 (PTS MN i 489))

**ID:** MN 73 (PTS MN i 489)

**Title (English, from literature):** The Longer Discourse With Vacchagotta

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāvaccha Sutta* (MN 73, PTS MN i 489; also known as the *Mahāvacchagotta Sutta*) is the seventy-third discourse of the *Majjhimanikāya* and forms the final installment in the collection's "Vacchagotta trilogy" [SuttaCentral; Bodhi, Revival of Bhikkhunī Ordination]. In this sutta, the wanderer Vacchagotta relinquishes speculative metaphysical questions to inquire directly into spiritual practice and realization [SuttaCentral]. Vacchagotta asks whether the Buddha alone has achieved awakening or whether his disciples have done so as well [Bodhi, Revival of Bhikkhunī Ordination]. The Buddha answers that far more than five hundred disciples have reached each spiritual level: ordained monks and nuns have achieved arahantship, celibate laymen and laywomen have attained non-returning (*anāgāmitā*), and non-celibate householders enjoying sensual pleasures have attained once-returning (*sakadāgāmitā*) [Bodhi, Revival of Bhikkhunī Ordination; Goodwin 2012; Radich 2007; Wen, Study of Sukkhavipassaka; Collett 2014]. Convinced by this complete spiritual community, Vacchagotta receives ordination as a monk under the Buddha [Bodhi 1970]. Following the Buddha's instruction to cultivate serenity (*samatha*) and insight (*vipassanā*) in close cooperation, he develops the higher spiritual knowledges (*abhiññā* / *vijjā*) and attains arahantship [Bodhi 1970; Saitanaporn 2009; Shonin et al. 2015]. Buddhaghosa's commentary on the sutta also analyzes the synthesis of *samatha* and *vipassanā* in relation to the *abhiññās* [Saitanaporn 2009].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral are found in the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* collections: SĀ 964 (T 99) and SĀ² 198 (T 100) [SuttaCentral; Shi Huifeng and Orsborn 2012]. SuttaCentral also notes a reference to the sutta in the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 14.8, *Abyākatakathā*) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus confirms the alignment with T 99 and T 100, while also finding extensive Pali-internal text reuse with stock doctrinal passages in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 5, AN 3, AN 10, AN 6), the *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 51, SN 12), and the *Dīgha Nikāya* (DN 2, DN 29) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus additionally aligns portions of the text with passages in Sanskrit and Tibetan works, including the *Daśabalasūtra*, the *Daśabhūmikasūtra*, and Prajñāpāramitā texts [DharmaNexus].
